blocks.prompt: 2. Find the general solution of the differential equation \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \left(\frac{1 - y^2}{1 - x^2}\right)^{1/2}\).
blocks.explanation:
The power \(\frac{1}{2}\) is a square root, so the right side is \(\frac{\sqrt{1 - y^2}}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\): a function of \(y\) times a function of \(x\). Separable.
Plan: separate, then use \(\int\frac{du}{\sqrt{1 - u^2}} = \sin^{-1}u\) on both sides.
steps:
Given: \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \left(\frac{1 - y^2}{1 - x^2}\right)^{1/2}\).
To find: the general solution.
Method: the equation is separable; separate the variables and integrate both sides with the standard integral \(\int\frac{du}{\sqrt{1 - u^2}} = \sin^{-1}u\).

Write the power as a square root
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\sqrt{1 - y^2}}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\]
Why: \(a^{1/2} = \sqrt{a}\) and \(\sqrt{\frac{p}{q}} = \frac{\sqrt{p}}{\sqrt{q}}\). We take \(|x| < 1\), \(|y| < 1\) so the roots are real and non-zero.

Separate the variables
\[\dfrac{dy}{\sqrt{1 - y^2}} = \dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\]
Why: divide both sides by \(\sqrt{1 - y^2}\) and multiply by \(dx\).

Integrate both sides
\[\int\dfrac{dy}{\sqrt{1 - y^2}} = \int\dfrac{dx}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\]
\[\sin^{-1}y = \sin^{-1}x + C\]
Why: \(\frac{d}{du}\sin^{-1}u = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - u^2}}\). One constant \(C\) is enough.

Check
Differentiate \(\sin^{-1}y - \sin^{-1}x = C\):
\[\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - y^2}}\dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}} = 0\]
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\sqrt{1 - y^2}}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\]
This is the given equation.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key (item 3) prints \(\sin^{-1}x + \sin^{-1}x + C = 0\). This is a misprint: it does not contain \(y\) at all, and even with the second term read as \(\sin^{-1}y\) the sign would be wrong (\(\sin^{-1}x + \sin^{-1}y = C\) solves \(\frac{dy}{dx} = -\frac{\sqrt{1 - y^2}}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\)). The correct general solution is \(\sin^{-1}y - \sin^{-1}x = C\).
